features.rationale: Job-relevant if defined from a job analysis and extracted accurately.
features.action: Acceptable in principle; confirm it is measured the same way for every candidate and is validated for this role.

features.rationale: Acceptable as a minimum; as an upper bound or a continuous score it becomes an age proxy.
features.action: Keep only with a written job-relatedness justification and a bias test of this feature.

features.rationale: Graduation year lets a model recover age almost exactly.
features.action: Remove unless a documented job analysis shows it is necessary for the role and an audit shows no adverse impact; if kept, test it explicitly.

features.rationale: In India a name often signals caste, religion, region and gender together. Audit studies have repeatedly found callback gaps by name.
features.action: Remove unless a documented job analysis shows it is necessary for the role and an audit shows no adverse impact; if kept, test it explicitly.

features.rationale: Residential segregation makes locality a proxy for community and income.

features.rationale: Career gaps are common after marriage, maternity, caregiving and illness; penalising them penalises women and people with disabilities.
features.action: Remove unless a documented job analysis shows it is necessary for the role and an audit shows no adverse impact; if kept, test it explicitly.

features.rationale: Legitimate only where the role needs the language; then test it directly rather than infer it.

features.rationale: Prestige of past employers compounds earlier inequalities of access.

features.rationale: Direct measures of job-relevant ability, given to every candidate the same way.

features.rationale: Scores inferred from faces or behaviour are affect inference (red line RL-01) and penalise cultural, neurodivergent and disabled candidates.
features.action: Remove unless a documented job analysis shows it is necessary for the role and an audit shows no adverse impact; if kept, test it explicitly.

limits: Keyword screening finds proxies that are named. It cannot find proxies hidden inside composite scores or learned from free text; only outcome testing by group (adverse_impact.py) can show those.
